bugs.what: Menu option numbers shift every turn (e.g. after an enemy dies or an item is consumed), so a number chosen based on the previous screen can silently map to a different action if not re-read carefully (I once meant to attack but hit 'use dried herbs' because the list had shrunk).
bugs.where: Barrow Crypt combat, and generally any combat/interaction with a dynamic menu

bugs.what: Pursuing one path to a hold's grief (the True Pardon for the Hanged Company) silently foreclosed an unrelated side quest (The Hidden Root) with no warning beforehand.

confusions: Finding a specific named sub-location (e.g. the Hundred Gallery, the Drowned Nave, the oath-stone) often required blind directional wandering across several unnamed rooms before the target appeared in 'get your bearings' — bearings is free and great once discovered, but it's easy to not think to use it right away in a new hold.

The permanence of crossing the Pass Gate ('17 threads... stay open for good') is only revealed at the gate itself, after most of the map has already been explored — a hint earlier (e.g. when Coldpass first opens) would help players plan which loose ends to tie up first.

It's not always obvious whether resolving a hold's grief via a 'bargain' counts toward the '3 hollows rested' win condition; status text clarifies this ('a bargain counts') but the in-scene choice text doesn't say so explicitly.
suggestions: Keep frequently-used actions (attack, talk, travel) pinned to stable numbers/letters across turns so menu shifts don't cause misclicks.
Surface a first-visit 'get your bearings' automatically (or a nudge to use it) when entering a new hold, since it's free and very useful.
Warn players earlier (e.g. at Coldpass' outer approach, not just the final gate) that crossing locks out unresolved threads permanently.
Label 'bargain' outcomes inline as counting toward the hollow-rested tally, matching what status already says, so the choice text and win-condition math agree.
